examBlueprint.tests: B2.2: the fluid-mosaic membrane, tonicity arrows, or a labeled cell
Interpreting scientific text; passage drawn from B2.2 (the fluid-mosaic passage)

standards.title: Cell structure and organization
standards.description: Students relate cell structures to functions and explain how compartmentalization and small size support cell function.
iCan: I can tell prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells apart and name what all cells share
I can name the major organelles and say what each one does
I can explain the endomembrane system as a protein-traffic path (nucleus to ER to Golgi to vesicles to membrane)
I can explain why cells stay small using the surface-area-to-volume ratio

standards.title: Membrane structure and selective permeability
standards.description: Students explain the fluid mosaic model and how membrane structure produces selective permeability.
iCan: I can describe the membrane as a fluid mosaic (phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins)
I can explain what makes a membrane fluid and list what membrane proteins do
I can explain selective permeability: what crosses the bilayer freely and what needs a protein

exam.examItems: MC Q4, Q5; SA 13, 14; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: Passive transport: diffusion, osmosis, tonicity
standards.description: Students predict the direction of passive movement across membranes and the effect of tonicity on cells.
iCan: I can define diffusion and facilitated diffusion and tell them apart
I can define osmosis and predict which way water moves across a membrane
I can use tonicity to predict whether a cell shrinks, swells, or stays the same in hypertonic, hypotonic, or isotonic surroundings
I can use the percent-mass-change versus molarity graph to find a cell's internal solute concentration

exam.examItems: MC Q6, Q7; SA 15; Part 3 CER

standards.title: Active transport
standards.description: Students explain how cells move solutes against their gradients using energy.
iCan: I can define active transport and explain why it needs energy
I can explain the sodium-potassium pump and the gradient it builds
I can tell primary active transport from cotransport, and active from passive transport

standards.title: Bulk transport: exocytosis and endocytosis
standards.description: Students explain how cells move large materials in bulk using vesicles.
iCan: I can define exocytosis and give an example
I can define endocytosis and tell phagocytosis, pinocytosis, and receptor-mediated endocytosis apart
I can explain why bulk transport needs energy and vesicles, and connect it to the endomembrane system
